title: Introduce fastpath fuse prober and slimline SLO medic
author: Evan Brooks
release_notes: Adds a low-risk probe that detects fastpath fuse failures and applies a short, observable routing bias to stabilize SLOs. Includes metrics and an ops runbook entry.
description:
Context: During a regional incident on 2026-02-14 we observed intermittent fastpath "fuse" failures where requests routed to the low-latency fastpath would trigger transient KV cache desyncs and then incur extreme tail latency. The incident engineering notes (SUP-4512) recommended an automated light-weight probe that can detect fastpath misfires and bias traffic to the slow/robust path for a bounded window rather than relying on coarse circuit flips.

What this PR does: Introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) a fastpath fuse prober (controlplane/prober) that periodically exercises a small synthetic request pattern against the fastpath and reports a concise probe outcome; 2) a slimline SLO medic (runtime/fallback_router) that consumes probe outcomes and applies a short-lived routing bias and shed recommendation when probe failure rate crosses threshold. Both pieces are intentionally conservative (short windows, backoff, and canary-only by default).

Key properties and motivations: - Minimize blast radius: bias window defaults to 10s and only affects up to 5% of matching tenant traffic (configurable per-tenant). - Observability-first: probe emits slo_medic.probe_duration_seconds, slo_medic.probe_outcome{ok,fail,timeout} and slo_medic.bias_applied_total with labels for region/model/tier. - Predictable behavior: Medic uses exponential cool-down and a sticky suppression to avoid oscillation; config maps include max bias duration and min probe samples. - Hotfixable: feature gate + runtime flags allow immediate disable; config is exposed via controlplane API and guarded by audit logs.

Changes included: - controlplane/prober/probe_controller.go: new controller, probe scheduler and small HTTP/GRPC harness for synthetic hits. - runtime/router/medic.go: bias decision logic, token-limited bias applicator and short-lived shed recommendations. - telemetry/metrics_registry.go: registered new probe/medic metrics + tagging. - docs/runs/ops/slo-medic.md: operational runbook with TTLs, alert tuning and rollback. - cmd/ctl/flags.go: feature-gate and defaults. - tests/prober_integration_test.go, router_medic_unit_test.go.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for bias decision and cooldown logic - [x] Integration test with synthetic fastpath misfire simulation - [x] Metrics and dashboard skeleton added - [x] Ops runbook and rollback steps - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag

Testing and validation: Local unit tests and integration harness ran. A dedicated perf job (perf/fastpath-fuse-prober) was executed in staging to validate no measurable QPS or latency regression for steady-state traffic. Canary rollout plan executed: 1% tenants for 6h, evaluated metrics, then 5% for 12h before full rollout. No regressions seen in canaries.

Rollout plan: rollout via feature flag: start in staging, then prod canary (1% tenants), observe slo_medic.* metrics and token rejection rates. If bias_applied_total > 0 and overall p99 decreases then proceed to 5% and 25%. Rollback via feature flag or controlplane toggle documented in runbook.

Related: SUP-4512 (incident), ENG-8092 (follow-up iteration), SRE-1203 (alert tuning).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add prober scaffold and scheduler; 2) implement medic decision logic and metrics; 3) tests, runbook and feature gate wiring
review_comments: Maya Patel: Can we tighten the default bias window from 10s to 5s for fast rollbacks? Concern about transient blips causing unnecessary shift.
Evan Brooks: I ran microbenchmarks; 5s increases oscillation risk. Kept 10s to ensure probe samples (min 3 per window). We can expose as runtime knob for rapid tuning.
Lars Jensen: Add a metric for 'bias_skipped_due_to_quota' so ops can see when tenant cap prevented biasing.
Evan Brooks: Added bias_skipped metric and unit test asserting quota behavior. Documented in runbook.
Priya Nair: LGTMed after CI green; please add a short dashboard for oncall to see probe trend and bias application per region.
Evan Brooks: Dashboard tiles added to team Grafana space (link in runbook).
notes: This PR was created as a hotfix after SUP-4512 and intentionally keeps conservative defaults. Operators should monitor slo_medic.probe_outcome and bias_applied_total for at least two full canary cycles.
